what_happened: The the person running Athena asked Athena to accept GitHub's CI result as proof that checks passed. The request did not say that the verdict's seen-commands rule (the D43 evidence rule) must also count a reused CI result as a command that was run. The first job checked this way, the disk fix, passed its checks but was rejected because the verdict rule did not see the commands. The the person running Athena had not traced how D43 evidence uses check records before writing the request. They then queued an urgent fix and stopped the drain so that other jobs would not be rejected the same way.
cause: Athena has no step that, for a request changing how check evidence is produced, lists the rules that consume that evidence and requires the reading to cover each one. The verdict's seen-commands rule is enforced in code but was written for locally run commands, and neither the request writer nor the reader is shown that dependency. The mismatch showed up only when a real job was rejected.
prevention: Add a check that runs before the first job under any change to check-evidence sourcing. It replays a known-good job whose checks came from a reused CI result through the verdict's seen-commands and D43 evidence rule. If the replay is rejected, the change is held until the rule counts reused CI results. Also add to the reading stage's required constraints that any request changing check-evidence sourcing must list every consumer of check records, with a criterion for each.
proposed_request: Make the verdict's seen-commands rule (the D43 evidence rule) count a check result reused from GitHub CI as a seen command, so a job whose checks passed through a reused CI result is not rejected for missing commands. Outcome: a job whose required checks are satisfied by a reused CI result for the correct commit and event passes the evidence rule, and a job with no such result or a result for a different tree is still refused. Acceptance: (1) a test built from the real check-record shape produced by the CI-reuse path shows the rule accepts it; (2) a test shows a CI result for a different commit is still refused; (3) the recorded evidence of job 20261101-102128-b1st is replayed through the rule and is accepted; (4) no other evidence rule is loosened. Priority: urgent. Then re-queue the rejected disk-fix job and resume the drain.
